summary: North Korea is essentially closed to tourism: the UK government says its borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and only limited tourism has restarted. It says tourists can normally travel only on an organised tour and independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs. US passports are invalid for travel there unless the US State Department specially validates them.

declarations.name: Arrival customs declaration
declarations.text: The UK government says foreign currency must be declared at customs, foreign mobile phones must be registered at the border, and GPS devices must be left with customs until you leave. It says customs officers confiscate literature or media deemed anti-government, subversive or pornographic, that further severe penalties including imprisonment are possible, and advises against bringing Korean-language or religious material.

source.name: UK FCDO — North Korea travel advice: entry requirements

currencyLimits.text: The UK government says there are no restrictions on bringing in or taking out foreign currency, but you must declare it at customs, and that importing or exporting North Korean won (KPW) is illegal. It says shops and restaurants usually charge foreign nationals in foreign currency, and some hotels may insist on full cash payment in advance.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — North Korea travel advice: entry requirements

notes: The UK government advises against bringing books or other written material in Korean, including anything religious, and says customs confiscate literature or media deemed anti-government, subversive or pornographic. Canada's travel advice says the same applies to material printed in South Korea.

The UK government says foreign mobile phones must be registered at the border and cannot connect to any network with an international SIM card, and GPS devices must be left with customs until you leave. Canada's travel advice says satellite phones and shortwave radios are confiscated on entry and usually returned on departure.

Ask your guide's permission before taking any photograph, the UK government advises; Canada's travel advice says photos or videos taken outside tourist areas can lead to confiscation of your equipment or detention.

payments.text: The UK government says credit cards and international mobile payments are not accepted; the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies, some places take Chinese yuan, and importing or exporting the won is illegal. Canada's travel advice adds that there are no ATMs, change in foreign currency is often unavailable, and some hotels accept credit cards with advance notice.

safety.text: The UK government advises against all but essential travel to North Korea. It says the North Korean authorities have previously detained foreign nationals for allegedly violating local laws and denied them access to support from their governments, and that a guide will almost always accompany visitors and decide where they can go. Canada advises against all travel, citing the risk of arbitrary detention.

tips.text: The UK government advises against all but essential travel to North Korea, and Canada advises against all travel, citing the risk of arbitrary detention. US passports are invalid for travel there unless the US State Department specially validates them.

The UK government says to ask your tour guide's permission before taking any photographs. Canada's travel advice says you must be accompanied by an official guide at all times, that material printed in South Korea or intended for religious proselytising may be seized, and that you can be arrested for unsanctioned political or religious activity.
The UK government says North Korea's borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and only limited tourism has restarted.

The UK government says a foreign mobile phone must be registered at the border and cannot connect to international or domestic networks with an international SIM card, and that lack of access to internet and mobile networks makes it almost impossible to communicate outside North Korea.

The UK government says the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies, with Chinese yuan taken in some places. Canada's travel advice says change in foreign currency is often unavailable.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for North Korea?
faq.answer: Yes, for every passport whose rule we found on an official page: the UK, Canada, Germany, France, Spain, Austria, the Czech Republic, Serbia, Türkiye, Singapore and China each say their own ordinary-passport holders need a visa; no official source we could read states the rule for other passports. The UK government says tourists can normally travel only as part of an organised tour, that independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and that the borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 with only limited tourism restarted. US passports are invalid for travel there unless specially validated.

faq.question: Can US citizens visit North Korea?
faq.answer: Not on a US passport unless the State Department specially validates it. The restriction comes from the US side: on 1 September 2017 US passports were declared invalid for travel to, in or through North Korea, the restriction has been extended every year since, and the latest notice runs it until 31 August 2027.

faq.question: Is North Korea open to tourists in 2026?
faq.answer: Barely. The UK government says North Korea's borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and that only limited tourism has restarted.

faq.question: Can I travel independently in North Korea?
faq.answer: Normally not. Canada's travel advice says you must be accompanied by an official guide at all times, and the UK government says the guide decides where you can go. The UK Foreign Office notes that tourists can normally travel only on an organised tour and that independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs.

faq.question: What money do tourists use in North Korea?
faq.answer: Mostly cash. The UK government says credit cards and international mobile payments are not accepted, that the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies with Chinese yuan taken in some places, and that importing or exporting the won is illegal. Canada's travel advice says cash is the most accepted form of payment and there are no ATMs, though some hotels accept credit cards if you give them advance notice.
